c.tagline: Ivory Coast's serene political capital, home to the world's largest basilica

taxi.fareNote: Shared woro-woro taxis run fixed routes for small flat fares; individual chartered taxis should have the fare agreed before departure, as meters are rare.

emergency.note: Emergency response can be slow outside the main hospital; the Yamoussoukro University Hospital Center (CHR) is the primary referral facility.

hood_landmark.Millionnaire: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace

avoid.reason: Petty theft can occur around the markets and quiet streets after dark, so avoid walking alone at night and keep valuables out of sight.

hood_desc: The city's showpiece district, built around the immense Basilica of Our Lady of Peace, a near-replica of St. Peter's in Rome commissioned by President Houphouët-Boigny.
The administrative heart of the city, home to government ministries, the Presidential Palace, and its famous lake of sacred crocodiles.
A planned residential district near the Félix Houphouët-Boigny Foundation golf course, quieter and greener than the city center.
An older, predominantly Muslim trading quarter with a lively market and the Grand Mosque, reflecting the city's northern Ivorian trade links.
A busy commercial and residential neighborhood centered on Yamoussoukro's main market, with small bars, eateries, and everyday shops.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water only.

transit.hours: Informal transit runs roughly dawn to 9-10pm, with limited service after dark
transit.pay: Cash fares paid directly to the driver at fixed low rates per route
transit.map: No official transit map; routes are learned locally or from drivers
transit.note: There is no formal transit authority; the city's wide boulevards mean much travel is by private car or taxi

air: Yamoussoukro Airport (ASK), domestic flights to Abidjan
train: No passenger rail service currently operating
bus: Intercity coaches (UTB, MTT) connect to Abidjan (~2.5-3 hrs), Bouaké, and other cities

tip.r: Tipping isn't customary, but rounding up or leaving small change for good service is welcomed, especially at hotels and restaurants used by visitors.
